text_segments: Custom fence building for privacy, security, and curb appeal. Cedar, vinyl, and chain link options for every budget.
A Well-Built Fence Defines Your Property and Your Privacy

Your fence is one of the first things people notice about your property. It sets boundaries, provides privacy, keeps children and pets safe, and adds real curb appeal to your home. In Snohomish County, where lot sizes range from compact urban parcels to multi-acre properties, the right fence makes a meaningful difference in how you use and enjoy your outdoor space.

At NW General Contractor, we build custom fences throughout Everett and Snohomish County. Whether you need a classic cedar privacy fence for your backyard, a durable vinyl perimeter for low maintenance, or a functional chain link enclosure for a specific purpose, we handle the full project from property assessment through final inspection. Every fence we build is engineered for the Pacific Northwest climate and installed to last.
We install and repair all major fence types used in residential and light commercial applications. Here is what we offer:

— The classic Pacific Northwest choice. Western red cedar is naturally rot-resistant, beautiful, and ages gracefully to a silver-gray patina. We build board-on-board, dog-ear, flat-top, and lattice-top privacy styles in heights up to 8 feet.

— Zero maintenance, weather-resistant, and available in a range of styles including privacy, semi-privacy, picket, and ranch rail. Vinyl will not rot, warp, or need painting, and most products carry a 20-year or lifetime warranty.
— Affordable, functional, and durable. Ideal for dog runs, property boundaries, garden enclosures, and utility areas. Available in galvanized or vinyl-coated finishes in green, black, or brown.
— Elegant fencing for front yards, pool enclosures, and decorative boundaries. Aluminum is rust-free and low-maintenance while providing the classic look of wrought iron at a lower cost.

— Storm damage, rot, leaning posts, broken rails, and sagging gates. We repair and reinforce existing fences to extend their lifespan and restore their function without a full replacement when possible.
— Single pedestrian gates, double drive gates, sliding gates, and self-closing pool gates. We build custom gates that match your fence style and include quality hardware rated for daily use.
— Rotted or broken posts are the most common fence failure point. We replace individual posts without removing the entire fence, using concrete footings and proper drainage to prevent future rot.

— Protect your cedar fence investment with professional staining and sealing. We clean the wood, apply UV-resistant stain, and seal against moisture to keep your fence looking great and lasting longer.
Fence Materials: Choosing the Right Option for Your Property

is the most popular fence material in the Pacific Northwest for good reason. It is naturally resistant to rot, decay, and insect damage without chemical treatment. Cedar is dimensionally stable, meaning it resists warping and splitting better than other softwoods. It accepts stain beautifully and ages to an attractive silver-gray if left untreated. For homeowners who want a warm, natural look that fits the PNW aesthetic, cedar is the gold standard. We source tight-knot and clear grades depending on your budget and visual preference.

is the best choice for homeowners who want a fence they can truly set and forget. Vinyl does not rot, crack, peel, or fade. It never needs painting or staining. Modern vinyl products have come a long way in terms of aesthetics and are available in wood-grain textures that convincingly mimic the look of painted wood. The initial cost is higher than cedar, but the lifetime cost is lower because there is zero maintenance.

remains the most affordable fencing option per linear foot. It is extremely durable, requires almost no maintenance, and provides reliable containment for pets and property security. Vinyl-coated chain link in black or green blends into the landscape more naturally than bare galvanized steel. For utility fencing, dog runs, and large property perimeters, chain link delivers the best value.
What Does a Fence Cost in Everett?

Fence costs are typically quoted per linear foot and vary based on material, height, terrain, and the number of gates. Here are the general ranges for residential fence installation in Snohomish County:
($15 – $25 per linear foot): Includes posts, top rail, fabric, and hardware. Vinyl-coated options are at the higher end of this range.

($30 – $50 per linear foot): Includes pressure-treated posts, cedar rails, cedar pickets or boards, concrete footings, and standard hardware. Height, grade of cedar, and fence style affect the final price.
($25 – $45 per linear foot): Includes posts, rails, panels, and hardware. Privacy panels cost more than semi-privacy or picket styles.
($40 – $70 per linear foot): Includes posts, panels, and hardware. Pool-code-compliant fencing with self-closing gates is at the upper end.

A standard 200-linear-foot cedar privacy fence typically runs between $6,000 and $10,000 installed. Gates add $300 to $1,200 each depending on size and style. We provide detailed written estimates that break down every cost before work begins, so there are no surprises.
A fence that lasts starts with proper planning and installation. Here is how we approach every fence project:

— We visit your property, discuss your goals (privacy, security, aesthetics, pet containment), review the terrain, and identify your property boundaries. If you do not have a recent survey, we strongly recommend one to avoid disputes with neighbors.
— We help you choose the right fence type, height, style, and material for your needs and budget. You will receive a detailed proposal with material specifications and a total price.

— Before any digging begins, we call 811 to have underground utilities marked. This is a free service and a legal requirement in Washington state. It protects against hitting gas, water, electric, or fiber optic lines during post hole installation.

— Posts are set in concrete footings at the correct depth and spacing. In the PNW, we pay special attention to drainage around posts to prevent premature rot. Posts are plumbed and leveled before the concrete sets.
— Horizontal rails are attached between posts to create the framework for the fence. We use galvanized or stainless hardware that will not rust or stain the wood over time.
— Pickets, boards, or panels are attached to the rails. We maintain consistent spacing, level tops, and plumb alignment throughout the entire run of the fence.
— Gates are hung on heavy-duty hinges with proper clearance and self-closing hardware where required. We adjust latches, stops, and closers for smooth, reliable operation.
— We walk the finished fence with you, check every section for alignment and quality, and clean up all debris and leftover materials from your property.
Timeline: How Long Does Fence Installation Take?
Fence installation timelines depend on the total length, terrain complexity, and the number of gates. Here is what to expect:
Complex installations with multiple gates, slopes, or corners: 1–2 weeks
Fence repair or partial replacement: 1–2 days

Weather can affect scheduling, particularly if we need to pour concrete footings during a heavy rain stretch. We schedule work to avoid curing issues and keep you informed of any weather-related adjustments. Material lead times are typically short for cedar and chain link, but vinyl and ornamental fencing may require 1 to 2 weeks for ordering depending on the style selected.
Permits for Fence Installation in Everett
Fence permit requirements vary by jurisdiction within Snohomish County. Here is what you need to know:
Fences over 6 feet in height generally require a building permit in the City of Everett and most Snohomish County jurisdictions
Fences in front yard setback areas may have height restrictions (typically 4 feet maximum)
Corner lots may have sight-line restrictions near intersections that limit fence height and placement
Pool fencing must meet specific code requirements including minimum height, gate hardware, and spacing between pickets
Some neighborhoods with HOAs require architectural review approval before installation

Standard 6-foot backyard privacy fences typically do not require a permit in most Snohomish County jurisdictions, but it is always worth confirming with your local planning department. We verify permit requirements as part of our process and handle any applications on your behalf.
Why Everett Homeowners Choose NW General Contractor

We build fences the right way from the ground up. That starts with proper post depth and concrete footings, quality materials sourced for the PNW climate, and hardware that will not rust or fail within a few years. We have seen too many fences installed by handymen or discount outfits that start leaning within two years because the posts were not set deep enough or the concrete was skipped entirely.

We are licensed, bonded, and insured in Washington state. We carry liability coverage and workers' compensation for every crew member on your property. We provide clear, detailed estimates, maintain clean job sites, and communicate throughout the project. If you want a fence built by a licensed general contractor who stands behind the work, give us a call.
What is the best fence material for the Pacific Northwest climate?

Western red cedar is the top choice for the PNW because it is naturally rot-resistant, insect-resistant, and handles moisture exceptionally well without chemical treatment. Vinyl is another excellent option for homeowners who want zero maintenance. Both materials perform well in our wet climate and last 15 to 25 years or more with proper installation.
How long does a cedar fence last in Snohomish County?

A properly installed western red cedar fence in Snohomish County typically lasts 15 to 20 years. With regular staining or sealing every 2 to 3 years, cedar fences can last 25 years or longer. The key factors are quality of the cedar, proper post installation with gravel drainage, and keeping the bottom of the fence from sitting in standing water or soil contact.
What are the property line rules for fencing in Everett?

In the City of Everett, fences are typically required to be set back at least 1 to 2 inches from the property line. The finished side of the fence generally faces outward toward the neighbor. Before installation, we recommend confirming your exact property boundaries with a survey if there is any uncertainty. We handle all setback and placement requirements as part of our installation process.
Do HOAs in Snohomish County have fence requirements?

Yes, many HOAs in Snohomish County have specific rules about fence height, material, color, and style. Some communities only allow certain fence types or require approval from an architectural review committee before installation. We recommend checking your HOA covenants before starting a fence project. We can help you navigate these requirements and build a fence that meets both your needs and your HOA rules.
How do I maintain my fence to make it last longer?

Cedar fences should be stained or sealed every 2 to 3 years to protect against moisture, UV damage, and mildew. Keep vegetation trimmed away from the fence to allow airflow and reduce moisture buildup. Vinyl fences require almost no maintenance beyond occasional washing with a hose or pressure washer. Chain link fences should be checked periodically for rust spots, which can be treated with rust-inhibiting spray paint.
Tell us about your fencing project and we will get back to you within one business day.
Ready to Build Your New Fence?
Call us today for a free on-site estimate. Licensed, bonded, and insured in Washington state.

text_segments: Professional flooring installation for every room. Hardwood, LVP, tile, and more — installed right the first time.
New Floors Change Everything About a Room

Flooring is one of the first things you notice when you walk into a home. Worn carpet, scratched hardwood, cracked tile, or outdated linoleum can make an otherwise well-maintained house feel tired and neglected. New flooring transforms the look and feel of every room it touches — and unlike a fresh coat of paint, a quality floor installation lasts for decades.

At NW General Contractor, we install all major flooring types throughout Everett and Snohomish County. Whether you are replacing the flooring in a single bathroom or doing a whole-house renovation, our team handles everything from subfloor preparation to final trim work. We help you choose the right material for each space, prepare the surface properly, and install it to manufacturer specifications so your warranty stays intact and your floors perform the way they should.

Every room in your home has different demands. The flooring that works in your living room may not be the right choice for your bathroom or kitchen. We help you match the right product to the right application. Here is what we install:

— Solid and engineered hardwood in oak, maple, walnut, hickory, and other species. We install nail-down, glue-down, and floating systems. Hardwood adds timeless warmth and significant resale value to any home.

— The fastest-growing flooring category for good reason. LVP is 100% waterproof, scratch-resistant, comfortable underfoot, and available in realistic wood and stone looks. Ideal for kitchens, bathrooms, basements, and homes with kids or pets.

— Durable, waterproof, and available in endless sizes, patterns, and styles. We install floor tile in bathrooms, kitchens, entryways, laundry rooms, and mudrooms. Large-format tiles, herringbone patterns, and heated tile floors are all within our scope.
— Wall-to-wall carpet for bedrooms, bonus rooms, and basement living areas. We install on quality pad with proper stretching and seaming for a smooth, wrinkle-free result that lasts.

— Rotted, water-damaged, or squeaky subfloors must be addressed before new flooring goes down. We replace damaged plywood, sister weakened joists, and ensure a solid, level base for any flooring material.

— Uneven subfloors cause flooring to crack, gap, or wear unevenly. We use self-leveling compound, grinding, or plywood shimming to create a flat surface within manufacturer tolerances before installation begins.
— Matching your new flooring onto stairways with custom-cut treads, risers, and nosing. We handle hardwood, LVP, and carpet stair installations with proper transitions and secure attachment.

— Electric radiant heat mats installed beneath tile, stone, or LVP. Heated floors eliminate the shock of cold tile on winter mornings and add a genuine luxury feel to bathrooms, kitchens, and entryways.
Flooring Materials: Choosing the Right Product

Selecting the right flooring material is one of the most important decisions in any remodel. The product you choose affects the look, the durability, the maintenance, and the long-term value of your home. Here is how the most popular options compare for Snohomish County homes.

has become the most popular flooring choice in the Pacific Northwest, and for good reason. It is completely waterproof, making it ideal for our damp climate where moisture can be a constant concern. High-quality LVP from brands like COREtec, Shaw Floorte, and Mohawk RevWood features a rigid core construction that resists denting and telegraphing subfloor imperfections. The wear layer on premium products (20-mil and above) can handle heavy foot traffic, pet nails, and dropped objects without visible damage. LVP installs quickly as a floating floor, keeping labor costs down, and it is comfortable underfoot with an attached underlayment.

remains the gold standard for living rooms, dining rooms, and primary bedrooms. Solid hardwood can be sanded and refinished multiple times over a 50-year-plus lifespan, making it the most sustainable long-term flooring investment. Engineered hardwood, which features a real wood veneer over a plywood core, offers better dimensional stability in our humid climate and can be installed over concrete slabs where solid hardwood cannot. Both options add measurable resale value to Snohomish County homes.

is the best choice for wet areas — bathrooms, showers, kitchen backsplashes, mudrooms, and laundry rooms. Porcelain is denser and more water-resistant than ceramic, making it the preferred option for floor applications. Modern porcelain tiles can convincingly replicate the look of wood, marble, or natural stone at a lower cost and with virtually zero maintenance. Heated floor mats pair exceptionally well with tile, which conducts warmth efficiently.
What Does Flooring Installation Cost in Everett?

Flooring costs vary based on the material selected, the condition of the existing subfloor, the square footage involved, and the complexity of the layout. Here are the general ranges we see for projects in Snohomish County:
($3,000 – $6,000 per room): Quality material and professional installation for a standard-sized room (150–300 square feet). Includes furniture moving, old flooring removal, and trim work.
($6,000 – $12,000): Engineered or solid hardwood installed in main living areas. Price includes subfloor prep, installation, transitions, and base molding.
($10,000 – $20,000+): Large-format porcelain, heated flooring systems, custom tile patterns, or whole-house flooring projects with multiple material types and complex transitions.

New flooring consistently ranks as one of the best home improvement investments. The National Association of Realtors reports that new flooring recoups approximately 100% to 147% of its cost in perceived home value. In the Snohomish County market, where buyers expect move-in-ready conditions, updated flooring can be the difference between a quick sale and a listing that sits.
Proper installation starts well before the first plank or tile goes down. We follow a methodical process to ensure your new floors look great and perform for years. Here is what to expect:

— We visit your home to measure the space, inspect the existing flooring and subfloor condition, discuss your lifestyle needs, and review your budget and material preferences. This visit is free and comes with no obligation.

— We help you narrow down options based on the room's use, moisture exposure, foot traffic, and your aesthetic goals. We can bring samples to your home so you can see how materials look in your lighting and against your existing finishes.

— Existing flooring is removed and the subfloor is inspected. We repair any damage, address moisture issues, and level the surface to meet manufacturer specifications. This is the most important step and the one most often shortcut by less experienced installers.

— Hardwood and some engineered products must acclimate to your home's temperature and humidity for 3 to 5 days before installation. We deliver the material early and store it in the room where it will be installed.

— Flooring is installed according to manufacturer specifications using the correct method for the product and subfloor type. We handle all cuts, transitions between rooms, and fitting around obstacles like cabinets, fireplaces, and doorways.
— Base molding, shoe molding, transition strips, and stair nosing are installed to complete the finished look. We match trim profiles and stain colors to the new flooring for a seamless result.

— We walk the completed floors with you, check every transition and detail, and address any items before we call the project done. We also provide care and maintenance instructions specific to your flooring type.
Timeline: How Long Does Flooring Installation Take?
Flooring installation timelines depend on the type of material, the scope of the project, and the condition of the existing subfloor. Here is a general breakdown for projects in Snohomish County:
Single room (hardwood with acclimation): 5–7 days total (3–5 days acclimation + 1–2 days installation)
Single room (tile): 2–4 days (includes setting and grouting time)
Whole house flooring (1,500–2,500 sq ft): 1–2 weeks
Projects requiring subfloor repair: Add 1–3 days depending on extent

We work room by room to minimize disruption to your daily life. For whole-house projects, we coordinate a sequence that keeps hallways and key rooms accessible as long as possible. We provide a detailed schedule at the start of every project and communicate proactively if any adjustments are needed.
Permits for Flooring Installation in Everett
Flooring installation generally does not require a permit in the City of Everett or Snohomish County. However, permits may be needed when the work involves:
Structural subfloor repairs that affect floor joists or load-bearing members
Adding radiant heated flooring that requires electrical circuit additions
Work that is part of a larger remodel involving plumbing, electrical, or structural changes

Standard flooring replacement — removing old material and installing new product on an existing subfloor — is considered a cosmetic update and does not trigger permit requirements. When permits are needed as part of a larger project, we handle the application and inspection process as part of our service.
Why Everett Homeowners Choose NW General Contractor

The difference between a floor that looks great on day one and a floor that still looks great five years later comes down to what happens underneath. Subfloor preparation, moisture testing, proper acclimation, and correct installation methods are the foundation of every lasting floor. We do not skip these steps, and we do not rush through them.

We are licensed, bonded, and insured in Washington state. We work with all major flooring manufacturers and follow their installation specifications to the letter, which means your product warranty stays valid. Whether you are refreshing a single room or replacing every floor in your house, we deliver clean work, clear communication, and results that hold up to real life in the Pacific Northwest.
What is the best flooring for homes with pets?

Luxury vinyl plank (LVP) is the best flooring option for pet owners. It is 100% waterproof, scratch-resistant, and easy to clean. High-quality LVP with a 20-mil or thicker wear layer can handle dog nails, spills, and heavy foot traffic without showing damage. Porcelain tile is another excellent option for pet-friendly homes, especially in entryways and mudrooms.
Is LVP better than hardwood flooring?

LVP and hardwood serve different needs. LVP is waterproof, more affordable, and extremely durable — ideal for kitchens, bathrooms, basements, and homes with kids or pets. Hardwood adds more resale value, has a warmer natural feel, and can be refinished multiple times over its lifespan. Many Everett homeowners choose hardwood for living areas and LVP for moisture-prone rooms.
How long does flooring installation take?

A single room typically takes 2 to 3 days including subfloor prep, acclimation time for hardwood, and installation. A whole-house flooring project usually takes 1 to 2 weeks. The timeline depends on the type of flooring, the condition of the subfloor, and whether furniture removal or trim work is included.
Can you install new flooring over my existing floor?

In many cases, yes. LVP and engineered hardwood can often be installed over existing hard surfaces if the subfloor is level and structurally sound. However, we always inspect the existing floor first. If there is moisture damage, unevenness, or structural issues in the subfloor, we address those before installing new material. Proper subfloor preparation is the most important factor in a long-lasting floor.
How much does heated flooring cost to install?

Electric radiant heated flooring typically costs $8 to $15 per square foot for the heating system, plus the cost of the flooring material and installation. For a typical bathroom, that adds $800 to $1,500 to the project. Heated floors work best under tile and stone, which conduct heat efficiently. They are especially popular in Pacific Northwest homes where cool, damp mornings make a warm bathroom floor a luxury worth the investment.
Tell us about your flooring project and we will get back to you within one business day.
Call us today for a free in-home consultation and detailed estimate. Licensed, bonded, and insured in Washington state.

More Than Parking — A Garage That Works for Your Life

A garage is one of the hardest-working spaces on your property. It protects your vehicles from the Pacific Northwest weather, stores tools and equipment, serves as a workshop, and in many cases can be converted into valuable living space. If your home lacks a garage, has a garage that is too small, or has a garage that could serve a better purpose, building or converting one is a smart investment.

At NW General Contractor, we design and build custom garages throughout Everett and Snohomish County. Whether you need a new detached two-car garage, an attached garage addition, or a full garage-to-living-space conversion, we manage every phase of the project from design and permitting through construction and final inspection. We build structures that match your home, meet code, and serve your needs for decades.
Garage projects come in many forms. Some homeowners need new construction from the ground up. Others want to improve or repurpose an existing garage. Here is what we handle:
— Custom-built detached garages in single, two-car, and three-car configurations. Designed to complement your home's architecture with matching siding, roofing, and trim details.

— Adding a garage to a home that does not have one, or expanding an existing single-car garage to a two-car. Includes foundation, framing, roofing, siding, and integration with the existing structure.

— Converting an existing garage into living space such as a bedroom, home office, family room, or rental unit. Includes insulation, drywall, flooring, electrical, HVAC, and egress windows to meet residential codes.
— New garage door installation and replacement. Insulated steel, wood carriage-style, and modern aluminum doors with electric openers, keypads, and smart-home connectivity.
— Converting an unfinished garage into a comfortable, usable space with insulation, drywall, lighting, and climate control. Ideal for workshops, home gyms, and hobby spaces.
— Dedicated circuits for power tools, 240V outlets for welders and EV chargers, overhead lighting, and subpanel installation. All electrical work done to code by licensed electricians.
— New garage floor slabs, slab repair, and floor coatings. We pour reinforced concrete with proper slope for drainage and can apply epoxy or polyurea coatings for a finished, easy-to-clean surface.
— Custom workshop configurations with workbenches, tool storage, dust collection hookups, dedicated lighting, and heavy-duty electrical. We design the layout around how you work.

Stick-built garages can be designed to match your home exactly — same roof pitch, same siding, same trim profiles. For homeowners on a tighter budget or faster timeline, pre-engineered truss packages speed up the framing phase while maintaining structural integrity.

Insulated steel doors with polyurethane core are the most popular choice in Snohomish County because they provide excellent thermal performance, resist denting, and are available in dozens of styles and colors. Modern aluminum and glass doors suit contemporary architecture and flood the interior with natural light.

What Does Garage Construction Cost in Everett?
Garage costs depend on size, site conditions, level of finish, and whether the structure includes utilities. Here are the general ranges for projects in Snohomish County:

($25,000 – $40,000): Standard 20x24 or 24x24 footprint with concrete slab, stick-built framing, composite or matching siding, asphalt shingle roof, one garage door, and basic electrical (lights and outlets).

($40,000 – $60,000): Same structure with insulated walls and ceiling, drywall, upgraded lighting, 240V circuits, epoxy floor coating, and a higher-end garage door. Suitable for workshops and hobby spaces.

($20,000 – $50,000): Converting an existing garage into a code-compliant living space including insulation, drywall, flooring, electrical upgrades, HVAC, egress windows, and potentially plumbing for a bathroom.

Adding living space above a detached garage significantly increases both cost and value. A garage with a finished apartment or ADU above can cost $80,000 to $150,000 total but adds substantial rental income potential or multigenerational living flexibility. In Snohomish County's competitive housing market, an ADU above a garage is one of the highest-ROI improvements you can make.
Building a garage is new construction, and we treat it with the same level of planning and professionalism as any addition or new build. Here is our process:

— We assess your property, discuss your needs, and create a design that meets your goals while complying with setback requirements, lot coverage limits, and building codes. We prepare construction drawings and submit permit applications on your behalf.

— The site is cleared, graded, and excavated for footings. We pour reinforced concrete footings and a slab with proper drainage slope. For sites with challenging soil or slope conditions, we engineer the foundation accordingly.
— Walls, roof trusses, and sheathing go up. The structure takes shape quickly during framing, and we schedule an inspection before closing in the walls.
— Roofing underlayment, flashing, and shingles or metal roofing are installed. We match the roofing material and color to your existing home for a cohesive look from the street.

— Siding, trim, fascia, and soffits are installed to match the house. Windows, if included, are flashed and sealed for weather protection. The garage begins to look like a permanent part of the property.
— Wiring is run for lighting, outlets, and any 240V circuits. Insulation is installed in walls and ceiling if the garage is being finished. Everything is inspected before drywall.
— If the garage is being finished, drywall goes up, the floor is sealed or coated, and any interior buildout (workbench, storage, etc.) is completed.
— The garage door is hung, the opener is mounted and programmed, and hardware is tested. We set up keypads, remotes, and smart-home integration if requested.
— We schedule the final building inspection, walk the completed project with you, and address any remaining items before we consider the project complete.
Timeline: How Long Does Garage Construction Take?
Garage construction timelines depend on the type and complexity of the project. Here is what to expect:
Detached garage (basic): 4–6 weeks from foundation to completion
Garage conversion to living space: 3–6 weeks

Permit processing in Everett and Snohomish County typically adds 2 to 4 weeks before construction can begin. Material lead times for custom garage doors, windows, and specialty items should also be factored in. We build realistic schedules and communicate any changes promptly.
Permits for Garage Construction in Everett
Garage construction always requires building permits in Everett and Snohomish County. Here is what triggers permitting requirements:
All new garage construction (attached or detached) requires a building permit
Garage conversions to living space require permits for change of use, plus electrical, plumbing, and mechanical permits as applicable
Electrical work (new circuits, subpanels, 240V outlets) requires a separate electrical permit
Concrete slab work may require a grading or foundation permit depending on scope
Structures exceeding lot coverage or setback limits may require a variance from the planning department

We handle the entire permit process from initial application through final inspection. Our drawings and documentation are prepared to meet the requirements of the City of Everett and Snohomish County building departments, which helps avoid delays and revision requests.
Why Everett Homeowners Choose NW General Contractor

Garage construction is real building work — it requires foundation engineering, structural framing, weatherproofing, and code compliance. This is not a project for a handyman or an unlicensed crew. We bring the same level of professionalism to a garage build as we do to a home addition because the construction process is fundamentally the same: permitted, inspected, and built to last.

We are licensed, bonded, and insured in Washington state. We design garages that complement your home's architecture, meet all local building codes, and serve your needs now and in the future. Whether you need basic vehicle storage or a fully finished workshop with future ADU potential, we build it right the first time.
Do I need a permit to build a garage in Everett, WA?

Yes. Any new garage construction, whether attached or detached, requires a building permit in Everett and throughout Snohomish County. Garage conversions to living space also require permits because they involve changes to the building's use and typically require electrical, plumbing, and insulation upgrades. We handle the full permit process including drawings, application, and inspections.
What is better, a detached or attached garage?

Both have advantages. Attached garages provide direct access from the house, which is convenient in the rainy PNW climate, and are generally less expensive because they share a wall with the existing structure. Detached garages offer more flexibility in size and placement, reduce noise transfer to the house, and can be designed with living space above. The best choice depends on your lot layout, budget, and how you plan to use the space.
Can I convert my garage into living space in Snohomish County?

Yes, garage conversions are allowed in most Snohomish County jurisdictions, though you will need permits and the space must meet residential building codes for insulation, egress windows, ceiling height, electrical, and ventilation. Some areas require that you maintain a minimum number of off-street parking spaces, which may limit conversion options on smaller lots. We evaluate your specific situation and advise on what is feasible.
Can I add a room or apartment above my garage?

In many cases, yes. Adding living space above a detached garage is one of the most popular ways to create an ADU (accessory dwelling unit) in Snohomish County. The garage must be engineered to support the additional load, and the living space must meet all residential codes including fire separation, egress, plumbing, and electrical. Zoning regulations vary by jurisdiction, so we verify what is allowed on your specific property.
What are the property setback requirements for a detached garage?

Setback requirements vary by jurisdiction and zoning classification. In the City of Everett, detached garages typically must be at least 5 feet from side and rear property lines, though some zones allow reduced setbacks for accessory structures. Maximum building coverage limits also apply. We verify the specific setback and coverage requirements for your property during the design phase to ensure full compliance.

text_segments: Outdoor Living Spaces in Everett, WA
Custom pergolas, covered patios, outdoor kitchens, and fire features. Extend your living space into the Pacific Northwest outdoors.
Bring the Indoors Out — Rain or Shine

The Pacific Northwest is one of the most beautiful places in the country, and there is no reason your outdoor space should sit unused for most of the year. With the right design — covered structures, integrated heating, proper lighting — your backyard can become a genuine extension of your home that you use nine or ten months out of the year. A well-built outdoor living space is where summer dinners happen, where you relax with coffee on a crisp fall morning, and where friends gather around a fire on a winter evening.

At NW General Contractor, we design and build custom outdoor living spaces throughout Everett and Snohomish County. From open-air pergolas and covered patios to full outdoor kitchens and fire features, we create spaces that are built specifically for the PNW climate. Every project is engineered for rain, designed for comfort, and constructed to last through decades of Pacific Northwest weather.
Outdoor living projects range from simple shade structures to full backyard transformations. We build it all, and we tailor every project to your property, your lifestyle, and your budget:

— Freestanding and attached pergolas in cedar, Douglas fir, and composite materials. Open-top designs for filtered shade, or solid-roof pergolas with polycarbonate panels for rain protection. Custom sizing, spacing, and architectural details to complement your home.

— Solid-roof covered patios that let you enjoy the outdoors regardless of weather. We build traditional gabled roofs, modern flat roofs, and shed-style designs with matching roofing and trim to integrate seamlessly with your home's architecture.

— Built-in grills, side burners, refrigerators, sinks, pizza ovens, storage cabinets, and bar seating. We build the structural framework, run gas and water lines, install electrical, and set countertops for a fully functional cooking and entertaining space.

— Custom gas and wood-burning fire pits, built-in outdoor fireplaces, and fire tables. We handle gas line installation, stone or concrete construction, and proper clearances for safe, code-compliant fire features that become the centerpiece of your outdoor space.

— Low-voltage landscape lighting, string lights on pergola structures, recessed lights in covered ceilings, step lighting, and accent lighting for pathways, plants, and architectural features. Good lighting extends usability into the evening and adds safety and ambiance.

— Concrete block, natural stone, and timber retaining walls for grade changes and terracing. Paver patios, stone walkways, and hardscape borders that define outdoor rooms and manage drainage on sloped lots.

— Enclosed outdoor rooms with screen panels that keep insects out while letting fresh air in. Ideal for dining areas, lounges, and three-season rooms. We build framed screen enclosures on existing or new patio structures.

— Reinforced concrete pads, electrical hookups, privacy screens, and access paths for hot tub installations. We ensure the pad is level, properly drained, and rated for the weight of a filled tub. Privacy enclosures in cedar or composite materials complete the setup.
Materials Built for the Pacific Northwest Outdoors

is the primary material decision for pergolas and overhead structures. Western red cedar is the traditional Pacific Northwest choice — it is naturally rot-resistant, dimensionally stable, and ages to a beautiful silver-gray patina if left untreated. Cedar accepts stain beautifully for homeowners who want to maintain the warm wood tone. Composite materials like TimberTech and Trex offer a lower-maintenance alternative that will never rot, warp, or need staining, though they cost more upfront and lack the natural warmth of real wood.
For covered structures, the roof design matters as much as the frame material. A
with asphalt shingles or standing-seam metal provides complete rain protection and can be matched to your home's existing roofing.

are a popular middle-ground option — they block rain while allowing diffused natural light to pass through, so the space does not feel dark on overcast days. For the PNW, we generally recommend solid-roof designs for primary covered patios because they offer the most weather protection and longest service life.
Outdoor kitchen materials need to withstand moisture, temperature swings, and constant use.

are the most durable options for outdoor kitchens. Stainless steel appliances and frames resist corrosion. We build outdoor kitchen islands with steel stud framing and cement board sheathing — not wood framing — to eliminate rot risk in the wet PNW climate. Stone veneer, stucco, or tile finish the exterior to match your design vision.
What Does an Outdoor Living Space Cost in Everett?
Outdoor living costs vary widely depending on the scope and complexity of the project. Here are the general ranges for projects in Snohomish County:

($5,000 – $15,000): A freestanding or attached pergola sized for a dining or lounge area. Cedar construction with optional polycarbonate roof panels. Price varies by size, material, and whether electrical (fans, lights) is included.
($10,000 – $25,000): A solid-roof structure attached to the house with proper roofing, gutters, and lighting. Size, roofing material, and ceiling finish (exposed vs. finished) affect the price.

($15,000 – $40,000+): Ranges from a basic built-in grill with counter space to a full kitchen with multiple appliances, sink, refrigerator, and bar seating. Gas line, water line, and electrical work are significant cost factors.
($2,000 – $8,000): A simple gas fire pit table starts around $2,000. Custom stone-built fire pits and full outdoor fireplaces with chimneys are at the higher end.

Outdoor living improvements typically recoup 50% to 80% of the investment at resale. In Snohomish County, where buyers actively look for homes that offer year-round outdoor usability, a covered patio with an outdoor kitchen can be a significant differentiator when your home goes on the market. These spaces signal a home that is designed for living and entertaining, not just shelter.
Outdoor living projects involve multiple trades and require careful planning to deliver a space that functions as well as it looks. Here is our process:

— We visit your property, discuss how you want to use the space, assess the existing conditions (slope, drainage, sun exposure, proximity to the house), and develop a design concept. We discuss materials, features, and budget to align expectations before any work begins.

— We evaluate soil conditions, drainage patterns, utility locations, and structural tie-in points if the project attaches to the house. For sloped lots, we plan grading and retaining solutions. For covered structures, we assess the best attachment method to the existing roof or framing.

— We prepare construction drawings and submit permit applications to the City of Everett or Snohomish County. Projects with covered roofs, electrical, gas, or plumbing each require separate permits. We manage the entire permit process and schedule inspections throughout construction.

— Concrete footings are poured for posts, columns, and any freestanding structures. Patio slabs and paver bases are prepared with proper compaction and drainage. Foundation work is inspected before framing begins.

— Posts, beams, rafters, and roofing go up. For covered patios, the roof is tied into the house properly with flashing to prevent leaks. Pergola framing is assembled, leveled, and secured. This is when the project starts to take its final shape.

— Gas lines for grills, fire pits, and heaters are run by licensed plumbers. Electrical circuits for lighting, outlets, fans, and appliances are wired by licensed electricians. Water lines for sinks and prep stations are plumbed. All utilities are inspected before being covered.

— Countertops are installed, appliances are set and connected, lighting fixtures are mounted, and all finish materials (stone veneer, stucco, tile, stain) are applied. Fire features are tested and adjusted.
— The new outdoor space is connected to the surrounding landscape with pathways, plantings, gravel borders, or sod. Drainage is verified to ensure water flows away from the structure and the house.

— We walk the completed project with you, demonstrate all systems (gas, electrical, lighting controls), and verify everything meets your expectations. Punch-list items are addressed before we close out the project.
Timeline: How Long Does an Outdoor Living Project Take?
Timelines depend on the complexity of the project and the number of trades involved. Here is what to expect:
Outdoor kitchen: 4–8 weeks (including utility rough-in and countertop fabrication)
Full backyard transformation (covered patio + kitchen + fire feature + lighting): 6–10 weeks

Permit processing in Everett and Snohomish County adds 2 to 4 weeks before construction can begin. Weather is also a factor — we schedule concrete and roofing work during dry stretches and protect unfinished work during rain. Material lead times for specialty items like custom stone, premium appliances, and fabricated countertops should be factored into the overall timeline. We build a detailed schedule at the start and keep you informed throughout.
Permits for Outdoor Living Projects in Everett
Many outdoor living features require permits in Everett and Snohomish County. Here is what typically triggers a permit requirement:
Any structure with a roof (covered patios, solid-roof pergolas) requires a building permit
Gas line installation for grills, fire pits, and heaters requires a plumbing/mechanical permit
Electrical work for lighting, outlets, and appliances requires an electrical permit
Water and drain lines for outdoor sinks require a plumbing permit
Retaining walls over 4 feet in height require a building permit with engineered drawings
Structures within setback zones may require a variance or special approval

Simple features like a portable fire pit, string lights on an existing structure, or a freestanding open-top pergola under a certain size may not require permits, but it varies by jurisdiction. We verify the specific requirements for your project and handle all permit applications and inspections as part of our service.
Why Everett Homeowners Choose NW General Contractor

Outdoor living projects involve structural work, roofing, electrical, gas, plumbing, concrete, and finish carpentry — often all on the same project. This is not a job for a landscaper or a handyman. It requires a licensed general contractor who can coordinate multiple trades, pull permits, manage inspections, and deliver a space that is safe, code-compliant, and built to last through years of Pacific Northwest weather.

We are licensed, bonded, and insured in Washington state. We have built outdoor living spaces on flat lots, steep hillsides, and everything in between throughout Snohomish County. We design for the PNW climate specifically — rain protection, proper drainage, moisture-resistant materials, and heating options that let you use the space year-round. If you want an outdoor space that is more than just a patio with a chair on it, we are ready to build it.
Can I use my outdoor living space year-round in the Pacific Northwest?

Yes, with the right design. A covered patio or pergola with a solid roof keeps rain off, and adding heaters, a fire feature, or a screened enclosure extends usability into the cooler months. Many of our clients in Snohomish County use their outdoor spaces 9 to 10 months a year with proper coverage and heating. The key is building for the PNW climate from the start, not trying to retrofit protection later.
What are the best covered patio options for the rainy Pacific Northwest?

For the PNW, a solid-roof covered patio is the best investment. Options include a traditional framed roof with asphalt shingles to match the house, a modern flat roof with a membrane system, or insulated aluminum patio covers for a lower-cost solution. Polycarbonate panels are a good middle ground, providing rain protection while letting filtered natural light through. We recommend a minimum roof pitch of 2:12 for proper drainage.
How much does an outdoor kitchen cost to build?

Outdoor kitchens in Snohomish County typically range from $15,000 for a basic setup with a built-in grill, counter space, and storage to $40,000 or more for a full kitchen with a grill, side burner, refrigerator, sink, pizza oven, and premium countertops. The cost depends on the size of the kitchen, the appliances selected, countertop material, whether gas and water lines need to be run, and the complexity of the structure housing the kitchen.
Do I need a permit for a pergola or covered patio in Everett?

In most cases, yes. Structures with a roof, including covered patios and solid-roof pergolas, typically require a building permit in Everett and Snohomish County. Open-top pergolas without a solid roof may be exempt depending on size and location, but it varies by jurisdiction. Any project involving electrical, gas, or plumbing also requires separate trade permits. We verify requirements and handle all permit applications as part of our service.
What is the ROI on an outdoor living space?

Outdoor living improvements typically recoup 50% to 80% of the investment at resale, depending on the scope and quality of the project. In the Snohomish County housing market, well-designed outdoor spaces are a strong selling feature because they extend the usable living area of the home. Covered patios and outdoor kitchens are particularly attractive to buyers because they signal a home that is ready for entertaining year-round.
Tell us about your outdoor living project and we will get back to you within one business day.
Ready to Create Your Dream Outdoor Space?
Call us today for a free on-site design consultation and detailed estimate. Licensed, bonded, and insured in Washington state.

text_segments: Interior & Exterior Painting in Everett, WA
Professional painting services that transform your home inside and out. Expert prep, premium paints, lasting results.
Fresh Paint Changes Everything About a Home

Nothing transforms a space faster or more dramatically than a professional paint job. A fresh coat of paint can make a tired room feel brand new, boost your curb appeal from the street, and protect your home from the elements. In the Pacific Northwest, where rain and moisture are a constant, quality painting is not just cosmetic — it is essential maintenance that protects your investment.

At NW General Contractor, we provide comprehensive interior and exterior painting services throughout Everett and Snohomish County. We use premium paints, invest serious time in surface preparation, and deliver clean, lasting results that hold up to the PNW climate. Whether you need a single accent wall or a complete exterior repaint, we handle every step from color consultation to final cleanup.

Every painting project has different needs. Some homeowners want a quick refresh. Others are preparing to sell or just moved into a home that needs a total color overhaul. We scale our services to match your goals and budget:
— Walls, ceilings, trim, doors, and closets. We protect your floors and furniture, cut clean lines, and apply two coats of premium paint for even, lasting coverage in every room.
— Full exterior repaints including siding, trim, fascia, soffits, and gutters. We power-wash, scrape, prime, and caulk before applying weather-resistant paint rated for the Pacific Northwest climate.
— A cost-effective alternative to replacing kitchen or bathroom cabinets. We sand, prime, and spray multiple coats of durable enamel for a factory-smooth finish that holds up to daily use.
— Cedar and composite deck staining, sealing, and restoration. We clean the surface, apply UV-resistant stain, and seal against moisture to extend the life of your deck in our wet climate.
— Driveways, walkways, siding, fences, and patios. Pressure washing removes years of moss, mildew, and grime and is often the first step before any exterior painting project.
— Patching holes, fixing cracks, skim-coating damaged areas, and matching existing wall textures. We make the repairs invisible before the paint goes on.
— Crown molding, baseboards, window casings, door frames, and decorative accents. Detail work that requires a steady hand and careful masking for crisp, professional edges.

— Not sure what colors to choose? We help you select palettes that complement your home's architecture, lighting, and style. We can provide sample swatches applied directly to your walls so you can see the color in your space before committing.
Premium Paints Built for the Pacific Northwest

The paint you choose matters as much as the skill of the painter. In the Pacific Northwest, moisture, rain, and limited sun exposure put unique demands on both interior and exterior coatings. We use professional-grade paints from Benjamin Moore and Sherwin-Williams because they perform consistently in our climate and offer the best color retention and durability.

For exteriors, we recommend 100% acrylic latex formulas with built-in mildew resistance. Products like Benjamin Moore Aura Exterior and Sherwin-Williams Duration provide excellent adhesion, resist cracking and peeling, and maintain their color despite months of overcast skies and rain. For homes in heavily shaded areas where moss and algae growth are common, we use coatings with antimicrobial additives to slow biological growth on painted surfaces.

Choosing the right sheen is also important. Flat finishes hide surface imperfections and work well on ceilings and low-traffic walls. Eggshell and satin are ideal for living rooms, bedrooms, and hallways because they are easier to clean while still providing a subtle finish. Semi-gloss is the standard for kitchens, bathrooms, trim, and doors because it resists moisture and wipes clean easily. We walk you through these choices so you get the right product in every room.
What Does a Painting Project Cost in Everett?
Painting costs depend on the size of the area, the condition of the surfaces, and the quality of materials selected. Here are the general ranges we see for projects in Snohomish County:
($400 – $800): One standard bedroom or living room including walls, ceiling, and trim. Two coats of premium paint, all prep work included.
($3,000 – $8,000): Full interior repaint for a typical 3–4 bedroom home. Price varies based on room count, ceiling height, trim detail, and the amount of prep required.
($5,000 – $12,000): Complete exterior repaint including siding, trim, fascia, and soffits. Includes power washing, scraping, priming, caulking, and two coats of exterior paint.

A well-executed exterior paint job is one of the highest-ROI home improvements you can make. The National Association of Realtors consistently ranks exterior painting among the top projects for cost recovery at resale. In Snohomish County, where curb appeal directly impacts buyer perception, a fresh exterior can add thousands of dollars in perceived value and help your home sell faster.
A paint job is only as good as the preparation behind it. We follow a detailed process that ensures clean results and long-lasting performance:
— We visit your home, discuss your vision, review the surfaces, and help you select colors and sheens. You receive a detailed written estimate with no surprises.

— This is where the real work happens. We sand rough areas, scrape peeling paint, fill holes and cracks, caulk gaps around trim and windows, and apply primer where needed. For exteriors, we power-wash the entire surface first.
— We mask off trim, cover floors with drop cloths, protect fixtures and hardware, and tape clean lines at transitions. Your furniture, carpets, and landscaping are fully protected.

— Two full coats of premium paint applied with brushes, rollers, or sprayers depending on the surface. We back-brush all sprayed areas for proper adhesion and use the right application method for each surface type.
— We cut in around fixtures, outlets, and trim with precision. All edges are clean and straight. Any spots that need attention get touched up before we consider the room complete.

— We walk the entire project with you, check every surface under good lighting, and address any punch-list items. All tape, drop cloths, and materials are removed. We leave your home cleaner than we found it.
Timeline: How Long Does a Painting Project Take?
Painting timelines depend on the scope of the project and the amount of prep work required. Here is what to expect for typical projects:
Cabinet painting: 1–2 weeks (includes cure time between coats)

Exterior painting in the Pacific Northwest is weather dependent. We schedule exterior work during dry stretches and monitor forecasts closely. Paint needs to be applied when temperatures are above 50°F and rain is not expected within 4 to 6 hours. We plan around the weather so you get a finish that adheres properly and lasts as long as it should.
Painting alone does not typically require a building permit in the City of Everett or Snohomish County. However, there are a few situations where permits or approvals may come into play:
Homes in historic districts may require approval for exterior color changes
HOA-governed communities may have color restrictions and review processes
Commercial properties may require permits for scaffolding or lane closures
Lead paint abatement (in homes built before 1978) must follow EPA RRP rules and may require certification

For residential painting projects, you can typically move forward without any permits. If your project involves drywall repair, electrical updates, or structural work in addition to painting, those components may require separate permits. We advise you on what is needed during your estimate.
Why Everett Homeowners Choose NW General Contractor

We are not a crew that shows up, slaps on a coat of paint, and leaves. We are a full-service general contractor with painters who understand that preparation is the foundation of a lasting finish. Our crews are experienced with every type of surface common in Snohomish County homes — from old-growth cedar siding on mid-century ramblers to modern fiber cement on new construction.

We are licensed, bonded, and insured in Washington state. We use premium materials, maintain clean job sites, and stand behind our work. If you want a painting contractor who takes the time to do it right, gives you a detailed estimate upfront, and delivers results that hold up year after year in the PNW climate, we are the team to call.
How often should I repaint my home's exterior in the Pacific Northwest?

In the Pacific Northwest, exterior paint typically lasts 5 to 7 years due to the high moisture, rain, and limited direct sun. Homes with south-facing or west-facing walls may need attention sooner. Using premium moisture-resistant paint and proper surface preparation can extend that timeline closer to 8 to 10 years.
What is the best paint for humid climates like Everett?

For humid climates like Snohomish County, we recommend 100% acrylic latex paints with mildew-resistant additives. Benjamin Moore Aura and Sherwin-Williams Duration are both excellent choices that resist moisture penetration and maintain color integrity despite the rain and humidity common in the PNW.
How long does interior paint last before it needs to be redone?

Interior paint in well-maintained homes typically lasts 7 to 10 years. High-traffic areas like hallways, kitchens, and kids' rooms may show wear sooner and benefit from higher-sheen, washable finishes. Bathrooms and laundry rooms should use moisture-resistant formulas to prevent peeling.
Why is surface preparation so important before painting?

Surface preparation is the single most important factor in a lasting paint job. Skipping prep leads to peeling, bubbling, and poor adhesion within a year or two. Proper prep includes washing, scraping loose paint, sanding rough areas, filling cracks and nail holes, caulking gaps, and applying primer. We spend significant time on prep because it determines how long the paint lasts.
What factors affect the cost of a painting project?

The main cost factors are the total square footage being painted, the condition of the surfaces (how much prep is needed), the number of colors and accent details, the type and quality of paint selected, ceiling height and accessibility, and whether any drywall repair or texturing is required before painting.
Tell us about your painting project and we will get back to you within one business day.
Ready to Transform Your Home with Fresh Paint?

text_segments: Patio & Concrete Services in Everett, WA
Custom patios, walkways, driveways, and retaining walls. Built to last in the Pacific Northwest climate.
Outdoor Living Starts with a Solid Foundation

Your outdoor space should be an extension of your home, not an afterthought. A well-built patio creates a place to grill, entertain, relax, and enjoy the Pacific Northwest summers that make all the rainy months worthwhile. Whether you are looking for a simple concrete slab or an elaborate multi-level patio with retaining walls and built-in seating, the foundation matters more than anything.

At NW General Contractor, we handle every type of residential concrete and hardscape project throughout Everett and Snohomish County. From new patio installations and driveway replacements to retaining walls that solve grading problems on sloped lots, our team manages the full scope — site prep, grading, forming, pouring, finishing, and sealing. We build it right so it holds up to decades of Pacific Northwest weather.

Concrete and hardscape work covers a wide range of projects. Some homeowners need a simple walkway repair. Others are planning a complete backyard transformation. We scale to fit your goals and your budget. Here is what we handle:

— The most versatile option for outdoor living spaces. Stamped concrete can replicate the look of natural stone, brick, slate, or wood plank at a fraction of the cost. We offer dozens of patterns and integral color options to match your home's style.

— Interlocking concrete or natural stone pavers laid on a compacted base. Pavers offer excellent durability, easy repair, and permeable options that help manage stormwater runoff — an increasingly important consideration in Snohomish County.
— New pours and full replacements for cracked, settled, or deteriorating driveways. We install with proper thickness, reinforcement, and control joints to minimize cracking over time.
— Concrete, paver, or flagstone pathways connecting your front entry, side yard, garden, or detached structures. We grade for proper drainage and ADA accessibility where needed.
— Segmental block, poured concrete, or natural stone retaining walls to manage slopes, prevent erosion, and create usable flat areas on hilly lots. Engineered designs for walls over four feet.
— Crack repair, leveling, overlay coatings, and decorative resurfacing for existing concrete that has seen better days but does not need full replacement.
— Front entry steps, back porch stoops, and garden stairs built to code with proper rise, run, and handrail connections. Poured concrete or precast options available.
— Exposed aggregate, acid staining, colored concrete, and broomed or troweled finishes. Decorative concrete adds character without the cost of premium pavers or natural stone.
Choosing the Right Material for Your Patio
The material you choose for your patio affects its look, its longevity, its maintenance requirements, and its cost. Here is how the most popular options compare for the Snohomish County climate.

is the most popular choice among our clients. It delivers the look of natural stone or brick at a lower cost per square foot, and because it is a single monolithic pour, it provides a smooth, consistent surface with no joints for weeds to grow through. The tradeoff is that cracks, when they occur, are more visible than with pavers. Proper control joints, adequate base preparation, and periodic resealing minimize this risk. Stamped concrete is ideal for patios, pool decks, and covered outdoor living areas.

are the premium option for homeowners who want maximum durability and design flexibility. Because each paver is an individual unit, the surface flexes with ground movement rather than cracking. If a section settles or a paver chips, you can lift and replace just the affected area without touching the rest. Permeable paver systems are also available, which allow rainwater to filter through the joints and into the ground below — a real advantage in the Pacific Northwest where stormwater management is a growing concern for residential properties.

is a classic Pacific Northwest look. The surface is poured like standard concrete, then the top layer is washed away to reveal the natural stone aggregate underneath. The result is a textured, slip-resistant surface with a natural, earthy appearance that blends well with Northwest landscaping. Exposed aggregate works particularly well for driveways, walkways, and pool surrounds where traction matters.
What Does a Patio or Concrete Project Cost in Everett?

Concrete and hardscape costs depend on the size of the project, the material selected, site conditions, and whether grading or retaining walls are involved. Here are the general ranges we see in Snohomish County:
($3,000 – $6,000): Standard brushed or broomed concrete slab, typically 200–400 square feet. Includes site prep, forming, pouring, and basic finishing.
($6,000 – $15,000): Decorative stamped concrete or interlocking pavers with a compacted base. Covers 200–600 square feet with color, pattern, and sealing included.
($15,000 – $30,000+): Multi-level patios, engineered retaining walls, built-in seating, fire pit pads, outdoor kitchen foundations, and integrated drainage systems.

Outdoor hardscape projects typically deliver a strong return on investment. According to the National Association of Realtors, a new patio recovers roughly 69% of its cost at resale. In Snohomish County, where outdoor living space is a major selling point, a well-designed patio can make your home stand out in a competitive market and extend your usable living area at a fraction of the cost of an interior addition.
We follow a structured process to ensure every concrete project is built on a solid foundation — literally. Here is what to expect:

— We visit your property, evaluate soil conditions, drainage patterns, and access, then discuss your vision and budget. We take measurements and photos to prepare a detailed proposal. This visit is free and comes with no obligation.

— We excavate to the required depth, establish proper grade for drainage away from your foundation, and compact the subbase. For projects on sloped lots, this phase includes cut-and-fill grading and any necessary retaining wall footings.

— We set forms to the exact dimensions and elevation, install rebar or wire mesh for reinforcement, and place control joints at the correct intervals to manage cracking. Expansion joints are added where concrete meets existing structures.

— Concrete is poured, vibrated to eliminate air pockets, screeded to level, and finished to the specified texture — broom, trowel, stamped, or exposed aggregate. Stamped patterns and integral colors are applied during this phase.

— Fresh concrete is covered or sprayed with curing compound to ensure it hydrates properly over the first 7 days. We keep traffic off the surface during this critical period. Rushing the cure leads to surface defects and reduced strength.

— Once cured, we apply a penetrating or topical sealer to protect against moisture, staining, and UV damage. We walk the completed project with you, address any punch-list items, and provide care instructions for long-term maintenance.
Timeline: How Long Does a Patio or Concrete Project Take?

Most concrete projects move quickly once site work begins. The biggest variable is weather — concrete should not be poured in heavy rain or freezing temperatures, so we schedule accordingly for the Pacific Northwest climate. Here is a rough breakdown:
Simple patio (200–400 sq ft): 3–5 days from excavation to finish
Stamped or paver patio: 5–10 days depending on size and complexity
Driveway replacement: 3–7 days including demolition of old surface
Retaining wall project: 1–3 weeks depending on wall height and length
Complex multi-element project (patio + walls + walkways): 2–4 weeks

All timelines exclude the 7-day curing period where the concrete must not bear heavy loads. We schedule pours to avoid rain in the forecast and can install temporary covers if needed. We provide a detailed schedule at the start of every project and keep you updated if weather or other factors cause adjustments.
Permits for Patio & Concrete Work in Everett
Not every concrete project requires a permit, but some do. In the City of Everett and Snohomish County, permits are generally required when the work involves:
Retaining walls over 4 feet in height (measured from bottom of footing to top of wall)
Grading that changes drainage patterns or moves more than 50 cubic yards of soil
Structures that encroach on setbacks or easements
Work within critical areas (wetlands, steep slopes, stream buffers)
New impervious surface that exceeds local stormwater thresholds

Standard patios, walkways, and driveway replacements that do not change the footprint or grading typically do not require permits. We evaluate permit requirements as part of our initial consultation and handle the application process when permits are needed.
Why Everett Homeowners Choose NW General Contractor

Concrete work is only as good as the preparation underneath it. We have seen too many patios and driveways fail prematurely because the base was not compacted properly, the drainage was not addressed, or the concrete was poured too thin. We do not cut those corners. Every project gets the right base depth, proper reinforcement, and correct finishing for the application and the climate.

We are licensed, bonded, and insured in Washington state. We work throughout Snohomish County and understand the local soil conditions, the drainage challenges that come with our rainfall, and the permitting requirements for each jurisdiction. Whether it is a simple patio for weekend barbecues or a full hardscape transformation with retaining walls and outdoor living features, we deliver work that lasts.
What is the best patio material for the Pacific Northwest climate?

Stamped concrete and interlocking pavers are the two best options for the Pacific Northwest. Stamped concrete offers excellent durability and drainage when properly sloped and sealed. Pavers handle freeze-thaw cycles well because the joints flex rather than crack. Both materials hold up to our heavy rainfall when installed with proper grading and drainage.
How long does a concrete patio last in Everett, WA?

A properly installed and sealed concrete patio in Everett typically lasts 25 to 30 years or more. The key to longevity in the Pacific Northwest is proper site preparation, adequate drainage, control joints to manage cracking, and periodic resealing every 2 to 3 years. Pavers can last even longer since individual units can be replaced if damaged.
How do I maintain my concrete patio?

Maintain your concrete patio by pressure washing once or twice a year to remove moss and algae buildup, which is common in the Pacific Northwest. Reseal stamped or decorative concrete every 2 to 3 years to protect the color and surface. Address any cracks promptly before water penetration causes further damage during freeze-thaw cycles.
Should I choose stamped concrete or pavers for my patio?

Stamped concrete is typically more affordable upfront and offers a seamless look with endless pattern options. Pavers cost more initially but are easier to repair since individual units can be lifted and replaced. Pavers also handle ground settling better and offer permeable options for drainage. We help you weigh the pros and cons based on your specific site conditions and budget.
Do I need drainage with my new patio?

Yes, proper drainage is critical for any patio project in Snohomish County. Our annual rainfall means water management is a top priority. We grade every patio to slope away from your home's foundation at a minimum of 1/4 inch per foot. For larger projects or sites with existing drainage issues, we install French drains, channel drains, or dry wells to manage water flow effectively.
